etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French methode, from Latin methodus, from Ancient Greek μέθοδος (méthodos).

definitions.definition: (countable) A process by which a task is completed; a way of doing something (followed by the adposition of, to or for before the purpose of the process).

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter III, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: He at once secured attention by his informal method, and when presently the coughing of Jarvis  […]  interrupted the sermon, he altogether captivated his audience with a remark about cough lozenges being cheap and easily procurable.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, William E. Conner, “An Acoustic Arms Race”, in American Scientist‎[1], volume 101, number 3, archived from the original on 17 July 2013, pages 206–7:
quote.text: Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.

quote.citation: c. 1599–1602 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene ii], page 261, column 2:
quote.text: Though this be madneſſe, / Yet there is Method in 't:  […]

quote.citation: 1980 December 6, “Mousie Mousie Wildflower (personal advertisement)”, in Gay Community News, volume 8, number 20, page 14:
quote.text: There's method in the universe.We're lucky that things aren't worse.

definitions.definition: (acting, often "the method") A technique for acting based on the ideas articulated by Konstantin Stanislavski and focusing on authentically experiencing the inner life of the character being portrayed.

quote.citation: 1989, Kenneth Branagh, Beginning, London: Chatto & Windus, →ISBN, page 64:
quote.text: In this case, the application of the famous method was a little shaky. To be fair, the director was dealing with a pretty stroppy cast.

definitions.definition: (object-oriented programming) A subroutine or function belonging to a class or object.

quote.citation: 2006, David A. Black, David Heinemeier Hansson, Ruby for Rails: Ruby Techniques for Rails Developers, Manning, →ISBN, page 101:
quote.text: When you call the method, you provide values corresponding to these variables in your method call.

quote.citation: 1809, Rachel Russell (baroness.), Letters. To which is prefixed, an intr. vindicating the character of lord ...
quote.text: "Says he, there is above ten thousand brisk boys are ready to follow me, whenever I hold up my finger : — Says I, how have you methoded this, that they shall not be crushed, for there will be a great force to oppose you?"

definitions.definition: (casting, by extension, transitive) To apply particular treatment methods to (a mold).
